items.detail: The **S&P 500 finished the week down about 0.1%** at 7,650.50 while the **Nasdaq gained 0.7%**, as the Fed delivered its first hike since 2023.
items.why: A unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% came with dot-plot projections signalling more increases and no cuts through 2027.

items.detail: The **Dow slid 1.7%**, a third straight losing week and its worst since March, with the damage in industrials, banks and consumer names.
items.why: A 5% risk-free rate reprices cyclicals and dividend payers hardest, while money stayed with AI-linked megacaps.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield touched 5.04%, its highest since 2007**, and closed the week back above 5% despite three straight days of falling crude.
items.why: A near-failed 20-year auction and the Fed's higher-for-longer message outweighed Brent's retreat from $109 to $103.87.

items.detail: Emerging market shares and currencies spent the week on the back foot as the **dollar index pushed above 100**, its highest in about six weeks.
items.why: The Fed's hike and a dot plot with no 2027 cuts widened the rate gap against emerging markets.

items.detail: The **Nifty fell 0.22% to 23,346**, a sixth straight losing week, though foreign investors finally turned buyers on Friday after **₹17,810 crore** of September selling.
items.why: Brent above $100 and a rupee stuck near 95.89 kept India's import bill and foreign outflows elevated all week.

items.detail: The **Russell 2000 lost roughly 1.25%** on the week, lagging large caps badly, while India's Smallcap 100 jumped **1.74%** on Friday alone.
items.why: Higher-for-longer US rates hurt debt-reliant small companies, while cheaper crude lifted domestic-facing Indian smaller stocks.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** fell below **$75,000** when the CLARITY Act died in the Senate, then rallied three days to an intraday high of **$81,034** on Friday.
items.why: Traders who shorted into the failed vote and the Fed hike were squeezed out by roughly $415 million of liquidations.

items.detail: **Ether ended the week near $2,603**, back from a post-CLARITY low around $2,404, even as its US ETFs lost money for three straight sessions.
items.why: Short covering rather than fund inflows drove the rebound, since allocators kept trimming Ether exposure.

items.detail: **Solana finished near $106**, the best of the majors, after dipping below $100 midweek alongside the rest of the market.
items.why: The SEC's five-year tokenised-stock exemption favours Solana most, since it already handles billions in weekly tokenised-equity volume.

items.detail: **Spot gold posted its first weekly gain in four**, recovering from a midweek low near **$4,262** to finish around $4,380.
items.why: Falling crude and a post-Fed drop in Treasury yields eased the inflation scare that had pressured bullion early in the week.

crossCuttingTheme: Oil set the week's direction and then handed it to the Fed: Brent's spike to $109 on the Saudi pipeline outage drove the 10-year to a 2007 high of 5.04% and forced a hawkish first hike, and even after crude fell back to $103.87 the dot plot's higher-for-longer path kept yields above 5% — punishing the Dow, small caps, the rupee and emerging markets, while gold and crypto rallied on the fading inflation scare.
